content.title: About
content.content: Honeydew melon (Cucumis melo var. inodorus) is a sweet, juicy variety with a pale green rind and light‑green flesh. Grown in warm regions worldwide, including the United States, China, and Israel. Raw honeydew is eaten fresh, in salads, smoothies, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Honeydew is composed of more than 90 % water, making it an excellent hydrating fruit.
Unlike many other melons, it has very few seeds in the flesh.
It is believed to have been first domesticated in ancient Egypt over 4,000 years ago.
The rind is rich in antioxidants, though it is usually not consumed.
Honeydew is often used in Asian cuisine to make cold soups and fruit salads.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Honeydew’s low calorie content makes it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber improves digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Beta‑carotene and other carotenoids protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to melons.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The natural sugars can be a concern for people with diabetes.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Improper handling may leave pesticide residues; thorough washing is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat honeydew fresh, cut into cubes or wedges. Add it to fruit salads, smoothies, yogurts, and dessert sauces. The flesh can also be frozen for homemade sorbet.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store whole melons in a cool place at 10‑15 °C for up to 5 days. Once cut, keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Discard if soft spots or off‑odors develop.
